summary.headline: Laurus Labs Q1 FY27 revenue rose 29% to INR2,026 crores, with EBITDA margin at 31.8% and CDMO up 69% to INR835 crores.
summary.overview: Revenue of INR2,026 crores grew 29% YoY, led by commercial supplies in CDMO and continued strength in Affordable Medicines. Gross margin was about 62.7% and EBITDA of INR644 crores at a 31.8% margin, up about 7 percentage points QoQ, as management attributed the gain to operating leverage and product mix. Profit after tax was about INR368 crores and ROCE about 19% versus 17.7% a year earlier. Management raised the FY27 capex guidance to about INR2,000 crores from INR1,500 crores, and net debt rose to INR2,656 crores with debt-to-EBITDA at 1.28x.

financial_highlights.change: about 3.3% higher than before (management's stated comparison)
EBITDA margin 31.8%, about 7 percentage points higher QoQ
management referenced FY26 vs Q1 FY27 comparison; Q1 vs Q1 clarification deferred offline

segments.name: CDMO (small molecule)
segments.commentary: Sales of INR835 crores, up 69% YoY, driven by late-stage clinical and commercial deliveries; about 55% of small-molecule CDMO revenue came from commercial supplies.

segments.name: Affordable Medicines
segments.commentary: Revenue of INR1,156 crores, up 10% YoY on higher volumes in ARVs and oncology. ARV revenue was INR669 crores (APIs INR415 crores, FDF INR254 crores).

segments.name: Laurus Bio
segments.commentary: Q1 sales about INR35 crores, up about 21% YoY. Phase 1 of the commercial fermentation facility (over 400 KL) is expected to be operational towards end of this year.

guidance_outlook: FY27 capex guidance raised to about INR2,000 crores from INR1,500 crores (earlier guidance of about INR1,000 crores); management said the increase reflects customer-driven capacity needs.
FY28 capex: management said last quarter's INR3,000 crores guidance for FY27 and FY28 has been changed, and it may exceed that, without giving a figure.
Gross margins expected to hold at similar levels in coming quarters despite some pressure from global conflicts.
Asset turnover target is a little over 1.0 (management says it is almost there); ROCE expected to rise from 19% and may reach about 23% over time.
CDMO to be at least 50% of revenue by FY30.

Krka JV: oncology facility ready early next year; solid oral facility in second half of calendar 2027; about INR400 crores invested so far with another INR400 crores needed, part of it from a partner loan.
Bio division: next 12 to 18 months seen as crucial; management needs 18 to 24 months to assess Bio and Crop Sciences opportunities.
capex_capacity: FY27 capex guidance raised to about INR2,000 crores; capex invested in Q1 was INR394 crores; cumulative capex has crossed INR4,700 crores per the analyst's figure.
Vizag site capacity expansion ongoing, plus commercial-scale peptide capacity being advanced based on customer demand.
Laurus Bio commercial fermentation facility: Phase 1 of a little over 400 KL expected operational towards end of this year; commercial start expected early next year per Q&A.
Krka JV oncology facility ready early next year; solid oral facility in H2 CY2027.
Final handover of 500-plus acres of land from the AP government in final stages.
demand_pricing: Management described strong demand for complex technology platforms and integrated manufacturing; customers want capacity in place before giving programs.
CDMO revenue is well diversified with no high customer or product concentration; predominantly innovator (on-patent) molecules.
Direct exports are about 55-60% of consolidated revenue.
ARV vs non-ARV mix is about 1/3 ARV and 2/3 non-ARV; management expects ARV share to fall further but not rise above one-third.
Custom synthesis run-rate expected to be maintained (within about INR100 crores either way) over next two quarters, per the analyst's framing that management accepted.
No customer advances received in Q1 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why was FY27 capex raised from INR1,000 crores to INR1,500 crores and then to INR2,000 crores within about six months?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the increase reflects capacity needed for existing customers' programs, including advanced intermediates and API, and new modalities in small molecules, and is tied to specific near-term partner needs.

qa_highlights.question: What share of small-molecule CDMO revenue came from commercial supplies, and is the non-commercial share sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: About 55% came from commercial supplies; the remaining 45% is mainly Phase III supplies, with one program already approved and expected to turn commercial soon.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Krka JV capex and timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR400 crores invested so far, with another INR400 crores needed, partly funded by a partner loan; oncology facility early next year and solid orals in H2 CY2027.

qa_highlights.question: Will CDMO margins improve, and what is the gross margin trend given raw material pressures?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross margin improved from 61% to 63% QoQ and was up about 3 percentage points YoY; management said margin pressure from global conflicts is not significant and expects similar margins going forward.

qa_highlights.question: Will CDMO be at least 50% of revenue by FY30, and what are the ADC revenue timelines?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is comfortable reaching at least 50% CDMO share by FY30; ADC programs are preclinical, with 3 to 4 years needed for Indian Phase I/II trials before meaningful revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Was there any ARV split or constant-currency growth clarification?
qa_highlights.answer: ARV API was INR415 crores and ARV FDF INR254 crores; constant-currency growth was given as about 2% YoY on an FY26 comparison, and management deferred the Q1-over-Q1 figure offline.

risks_watch: Capex intensity: FY27 capex of about INR2,000 crores plus FY28 may exceed INR3,000 crores, with net debt rising to INR2,656 crores and ROCE dependent on utilisation.
Lumpiness of CDMO orders, with 45% of small-molecule CDMO revenue from non-commercial (Phase III/launch) supplies that may pause after inventory build.
Gross margin pressure from raw material costs linked to Middle East/West Asia conflict.
Bio and new modalities (ADC, gene therapy, peptides) remain pre-revenue or early; R&D at 5.8% of revenue, up about 70% YoY.
Operating cash flow not disclosed; management to revert offline. Constant-currency growth figure was also clarified only partially on the call.
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansive on CDMO growth and capex, with a clear conviction on the FY30 50% CDMO target. Evasive on granular disclosures (product-wise revenue, CDMO TAM, separate CDMO ROCE, operating cash flow), citing confidentiality.
key_quotes: We reported signif icant acceleration in our CDMO business, maintained sustained momentum in affordable medicine portfolio, and continue to show tangible advancement in our mid - and late -stage commercial projects with global innovators.
So now our capex investment is very heavy because we were able to predict better than earlier.
At this point, we are very comfortable to say that by FY '30, we will definitely reach our target of at least 50% of revenue come from CDMO segment.
Our CDMO business is well diversified. No product or no customer are contributing significantly in our business.

Krka JV solid oral facility (H2 CY2027)

growth.why: Q1 revenue grew 29% YoY to INR2,026 crores and FY27 capex was raised to about INR2,000 crores (from INR1,500 crores) tied to customer capacity needs, with CDMO targeted at 50%+ of revenue by FY30, but no explicit FY27 revenue growth number was given and the new capacity (Bio fermentation, Krka JV) only comes online in 2 to 3 quarters, so backing is partial.
